questions.q: What is the main difference between the two?
options: Cross: image asks and text answers. Joint: image and text join one sequence, and both change
Cross updates the text, and joint doesn't
questions.answer: Cross: image asks and text answers. Joint: image and text join one sequence, and both change
questions.why: CrossAttention takes q from x and k, v from context. _block_mixing joins q, k, v, then splits.

questions.q: Why does a U-Net block also have self-attention?
options: Cross-attention alone never lets image tokens see each other
questions.answer: Cross-attention alone never lets image tokens see each other
questions.why: The lab: changing image token 3 doesn't move image token 0 under cross.

questions.q: In SD 1.5, do the text rows change between blocks?
options: No, the same rows are used throughout
questions.answer: No, the same rows are used throughout
questions.why: attn2 reads the context and returns only x's update.

questions.q: After their double blocks, what does Flux do with the two streams?
options: Joins them for good, for single blocks
questions.answer: Joins them for good, for single blocks
questions.why: The model's SingleStreamBlocks work on one sequence.

questions.q: A node written for U-Net attn1 is used on Flux. What is a real risk?
options: It does nothing, with no error
questions.answer: It does nothing, with no error
questions.why: Flux reads block patches under dit, not attn1. CU-322 has an example.

questions.q: From the lab's pair counts at this size, where does most of the cost sit in both designs?
questions.why: 16.78 million of 17 to 21 million pairs in one block are image to image.
